summary: Frontend-only smoke + integration test of the redesigned Awwwards-tier portfolio. Verified intro loader, hero heading/typewriter, navbar shrink, section-level testids, achievements count-up, contact links, EmailJS fallback, theme toggle, custom cursor, background-fx, scroll-progress bar, mobile drawer open/close, and no horizontal overflow at 320/375/390/768/1024/1440px.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking footer-top-link (href=#top) does not scroll to y=0; ended at scrollY=745. Likely because the fixed navbar offset causes the anchor jump to stop mid-page (id=top on <section class='hero container'> sits below hidden padding). Consider using window.scrollTo({top:0}) or moving id='top' to a zero-position wrapper.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Fix footer 'Back to top' so it scrolls fully to window top instead of ~745px.

NOTE: Review request references data-testid values that differ from implementation: 'nav-active-pill' is a framer-motion layoutId + className, not a data-testid (visual pill works). 'tl-item*/tl-progress' are implemented as 'experience-item-1..3' + 'experience-timeline'. Project cards are 'project-01..04' (not 'project-card'). Contact links are 'email-link/phone-link/linkedin-link/github-link' (not 'contact-email/phone/...'). Theme toggle is 'theme-toggle-button'. Back-to-top is 'footer-top-link'. Consider aligning either the spec or the testids for future test runs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Wait >=4.5s after page load before asserting hero. Use ACTUAL testids from code, not spec: experience-item-1..3, experience-timeline, project-01..04, email-link, phone-link, linkedin-link, github-link, theme-toggle-button, footer-top-link. CountUp targets: codechef=3 in 1.6s, leetcode=176 in 2.2s (scroll to achievements-section to trigger). Mobile 390 drawer closes on link click (verified). No horizontal overflow at any width tested.
rca_of_the_issue: Back-to-top anchor scrolls to element id='top' on <section class='hero container'>. The container has top padding pushing content down; anchor target y is above content but the browser's smooth-scroll target seems to resolve to an intermediate offset (measured 745px). Programmatic scrollTo(0,0) would eliminate this.
